evals.prompt: /to-tickets Spec: add 'saved searches' to our job board. Users can save a search (filters + keyword), see them in a sidebar, rename/delete them, and opt into a daily email digest of new matches. Stack: Rails + Postgres + React. Tracker is local markdown in .scratch/.
evals.expected_output: Drafts tracer-bullet vertical slices with blocking edges, quizzes the user on granularity/edges, then writes one file per ticket under .scratch/saved-searches/issues/NN-slug.md.
expectations: Tickets are vertical slices cutting through schema, API, UI and tests (e.g. 'save a search and see it in the sidebar'), not horizontal layers like 'create DB tables' / 'build API' / 'build UI'
Each ticket lists Title, Blocked by (or 'None — can start immediately'), and What it delivers
Asks the user whether granularity is right, whether blocking edges are correct, and whether to merge/split tickets before publishing
Publishes one file per ticket at .scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md numbered from 01 in dependency order, never a single combined file
Each local ticket has 'What to build', 'Blocked by', 'Status: ready-for-agent', and checkbox acceptance criteria

evals.prompt: /to-tickets We need to rename the `customer_id` column to `account_id` across the whole monorepo — it's referenced in ~3,000 places across packages/billing, packages/crm, packages/reporting and the GraphQL schema. Tracker is GitHub.
evals.expected_output: Recognises a wide refactor and sequences it as expand-contract tickets with migrate batches per package, published as GitHub issues with native blocking links.
expectations: Identifies this as a wide refactor (large blast radius) that should not be forced into tracer-bullet vertical slices

Sequences it as expand–contract: an expand ticket adding account_id alongside customer_id, migrate tickets batched per package each blocked by expand, and a contract ticket blocked by every migrate batch
Publishes GitHub issues in dependency order (blockers first) using native blocking/sub-issue relationships where available
Applies the ready-for-agent label to the tickets
Presents the breakdown for user approval before publishing

evals.prompt: /to-tickets #214 — that's the spec issue for multi-currency pricing on our GitHub repo. Break it down.
evals.expected_output: Fetches issue #214 with comments, proposes vertical tickets with blocking edges (prefactoring first), quizzes the user, then creates GitHub issues referencing #214 as parent without modifying it.
expectations: Fetches and reads the full body and comments of issue #214 before drafting
Looks for prefactoring opportunities and places any prefactor ticket first, blocking the dependent slices
Each GitHub issue follows the template with Parent (referencing #214), What to build, Acceptance criteria, and Blocked by sections
Explicitly does not close or modify the parent issue #214
Avoids specific file paths and code snippets in ticket bodies
